output.brief: The departures are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, against 1 of 13 who never worked on it. Other groups' attrition is normal, and the billable-target rise applied to all groups, so neither general market mobility nor the target change explains this. But every Kestrel associate was supervised by Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no one else. The heavy workload and his supervision therefore cannot be told apart in the records. The survey comments point to both. Pay is mentioned but not shown to drive exits. Exit forms say 'career opportunity', but leavers knew the group head might see them, so they are weak evidence. I am not confident enough to say which factor matters most. Don't pay the £12k retention bonus and close the review: it could cost £228k, and it leaves the likely cause untouched. Instead commission the roughly £9k confidential interviews, using an outside interviewer, structured to separate supervision from workload. Four leavers have already agreed to take part. Also add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Decide on moving supervision or bringing in contract reviewers once the interviews are done. Kestrel's heavy review phase runs to December, so move quickly.
